answer: A physical unclonable function in the chip answers challenges with responses determined by microscopic manufacturing variations. The agent registers by answering a random PUF challenge, and verifiers check the response against the enrolled pattern. An orchard of enrolled responses grows with each registration, and a canyon separates genuine PUF answers from modeled ones. A mesa of recorded patterns lets verifiers spot reuse. Modeling the PUF is infeasible, so one chip means one identity.
